analysis: All three changes are documentation-only, and I found no security regression. docs/provider/hardware-requirements.md adds a note (head lines 13-15) that Nemotron Super VL has no qualified RAM tier or serving recommendation and that its unregistered native builder is an internal qualification path. That wording is conservative and does not claim any new qualification. docs/reference/README.md only adds an index link at head line 10 to nemotron-super-image-formats.md. That target file is not in the supplied evidence, so I could not examine it. docs/reference/configuration.md adds four env vars at head lines ~320-323: DARKBLOOM_NEMOTRON_SUPER_MTP, _MTP_DEPTH, _MTP_VERIFICATION and _MAX_CONCURRENT. The documented behavior is that they are opt-in, off by default, and not forwarded to LaunchAgents, so a background daemon is unaffected. Invalid values fail the load rather than falling back silently, and the MTP-enabled owner refuses media. They are local-process env knobs on the provider, in the TB-007 / TB-003 operator domain, where the operator already controls the process. The settings add no wire, attestation, authorization or encryption surface. The documented limits are bounded (depth 1-3, concurrency 1-64) and no behavior is claimed that bypasses the admission gates. I did not read the Swift implementations (NemotronSuperLocalMTP.swift, NemotronSuperLocalAdmission.swift), so this review does not confirm that the code matches the documented bounds. Concurrency up to 64 is a capacity/DoS concern for the operator's own machine (T-029-adjacent), but the docs say the KV grant must hold every request's fixed bytes. No threat-model update is needed beyond possibly noting the unpublished Super owner if it later ships. The visible file_changes patch excerpt for configuration.md is truncated, so the MAX_CONCURRENT row was reviewed from the patch unit instead, which is complete.
